Sets discount approval authority for direct enterprise sales for calendar 2025.

This policy is effective from 2025-01-01 through 2025-12-31.

# Approval Authority Matrix — Enterprise Discounts (2026)

Applies to discount requests governed by the Northstar Pricing Policy 2026.

| Role | Discount authority |
|---|---|
| Enterprise Account Executive | ≤10% |
| VP Sales | >10% and ≤20% |
| Chief Revenue Officer | >20% |

Yes. The decision on DR-9001 was valid under the rules in force when it was made.

**The decision:** Decision record DEC-2026-0001 approved Sarah Chen's request for 15% off the NS-500 Industrial Controller for Acme Manufacturing. The request is dated 2026-09-23, and the record gives the outcome as "approve with authorization". Michael Torres approved it as VP Sales on 2026-09-24.

**Rules in force at the time:** Northstar Pricing Policy 2026 and the Approval Authority Matrix APP-MATRIX-2026. Both ran from 2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31.
- Enterprise Account Executives could approve up to 10%. Sarah Chen is an Enterprise Account Executive, so she couldn't approve 15% herself.
- Discounts above 10% and up to 20% needed the VP Sales. A 15% discount falls in that band.
- The matrix says approval authority belongs to the role, not the person.

**Who approved it:** The employee list and org chart show Michael Torres as VP Sales, reporting to the Chief Revenue Officer, David Morgan. The knowledge base has no role change for him, so he held the role that the rules required. One caveat: his VP Sales role isn't dated in the records, so this relies on the current employee list and org chart.

**Whether Acme qualified for 15%:** Acme's supply agreement (ACME-MFG-2025) and its pricing exception EXC-ACME-NS500-15 both run from 2025-04-01 to 2028-03-31. The exception covers the NS-500 only, allows up to 15%, and was approved by the CRO on 2025-03-20. It replaced the older 10% exception. So 15% was the most Acme could get, and it was allowed. The exception says it doesn't give anyone approval authority, and the decision didn't treat it as if it did: approval still went through the VP Sales.

**Two points to note:**
- As of today (2027-02-01), Pricing Policy 2027 is in force. Under it, anything above 12% needs the Chief Revenue Officer, so the same request made now would need CRO approval. That doesn't change the 2026 decision, because the 2027 policy only covers requests dated on or after 2027-01-01.
- The discount-request spreadsheet still shows DR-9001 as "Pending", although the decision record says it was approved on 2026-09-24. The spreadsheet looks like an older snapshot and may need updating.
